fix: resolve reply.mediaType from raw response headers (#7054)

#### Description

When inspecting `reply.mediaType`, the getter in `lib/reply.js` directly
accessed `this[kReplyHeaders]['content-type']`.

However, `reply.getHeader()`, `reply.hasHeader()`, `reply.getHeaders()`,
and `reply.send()` (line 177:
`ContentType.from(this.getHeader('content-type'))`) all resolve headers
from both Fastify's internal reply headers (`this[kReplyHeaders]`) and
fallback to Node's raw response headers (`this.raw.getHeader(key)`).

If a plugin, hook, or middleware sets the content type on `reply.raw`
(e.g. `reply.raw.setHeader('content-type', 'application/json')`):
- `reply.getHeader('content-type')` returns `'application/json'`.
- `reply.send()` parses
`ContentType.from(this.getHeader('content-type'))`.
- But `reply.mediaType` returned `undefined`.

This updates the `mediaType` getter in `lib/reply.js` to read
`this.getHeader('content-type')`, aligning it with `reply.send()` and
properly supporting hea

fix(router): use non-capturing groups for optional static segments in compilePath (#15200)

* fix(router): use non-capturing groups for optional static segments in compilePath

When a route path contains optional static segments (e.g. `/school?/user/:id`),
compilePath was generating capturing groups `(\/school)?` for those segments.
This shifted the capture group indices used to extract dynamic params, causing
matchPath to return wrong param values — e.g. `params.id` would be `"/school"`
instead of the correct value.

Additionally, consecutive optional static segments (e.g. `/one?/two?`) were only
partially handled: only the first optional segment was wrapped in an optional
group because the global regex consumed the `/` separator. Subsequent segments'
`?` were left as unescaped regex quantifiers, making the last letter of the
segment optional in the regex rather than the whole segment.

fix(content): invalidate the data store directly on write (#17755)

The dev server relied on the file watcher observing the atomic rename
that commits a data store write to invalidate the content virtual
modules. On Windows the watcher can miss that event, leaving dev
serving stale content until a restart (#17335). The store now notifies
listeners after real disk writes and the dev server invalidates
directly, keeping the watcher path as a fallback for other processes
with echo suppression to avoid double reloads.

request:
Fix glob() loader watcher ignoring negation patterns, causing unrelated files to be ingested (#17510)

* fix(content): split negation patterns in glob loader watcher to match tinyglobby semantics (#17484)

The glob loader's `matchesGlob` function used `picomatch.isMatch(entry, pattern)` with the
full pattern array. When the array contained negation patterns like `!docs/drafts/**`,
picomatch treated each pattern independently (union semantics), so the negation matched
every path outside `docs/drafts/` — causing unrelated files (e.g. `.astro/data-store.json`)
to be ingested as collection entries.

This created a feedback loop where the data store re-ingested itself on every write,
growing unboundedly.

Fix: split the pattern array into positive patterns and negations, passing negations
via picomatch's `ignore` option to match tinyglobby/fast-glob's set-subtraction semantics
used in the initial scan.

* Add changeset for glob() loader watcher negation fix

request:
fix(ws): stop reading from a client that does not read its replies

WsAdapter sent every reply without looking at how much was already
queued for the client, and went on reading and handling its messages.
A client that wrote many requests to a handler with a large reply and
read nothing made the server queue all the replies, thousands of times
what it sent, until the process ran out of memory.

The adapter now pauses a client while more than 1 MB of replies are
queued for it, or while its messages wait for a free slot, and resumes
it once its replies are written out. A client with more than 128 MB
queued for it, e.g. from Observables a handler returned or from what
exception filters sent, is disconnected. The new maxSendBufferSize
option changes that limit, and 0 lifts it. A client that is slow to
read now has its messages read more slowly as well.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-EXUZYA5M.
summary: Fixed later by aae7cb0: fix(ws): keep a client paused while any gateway on it is backlogged

request:
fix(ws): keep a client paused while any gateway on it is backlogged

Gateways that share a server each bind their handlers to the same
client, and each kept its own record of whether it had paused the
client. ws has a single paused state per client, so when two gateways
paused one client, the first to catch up resumed it while the other
still had messages waiting. That gateway never paused the client again,
and the list of its messages waiting for a free slot grew for as long
as the client kept sending.

The adapter now counts, per client, how many gateways hold it back, and
resumes it only once none does. With several gateways on one server, a
client whose messages keep one gateway busy is no longer read from for
the others either, as already happens for the events of one gateway.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-36006GKO.
summary: fix(ws): keep a client paused while any gateway on it is backlogged

request:
fix(core): drop an overlapped middleware route only when it is covered

removeOverlappedRoutes() dropped any route whose path matched a regex
built by hand from a sibling ":param" route, so that the middleware ran
once for them. That regex matched more than the sibling's mount: it
swallowed text after a parameter (":id.json"), read pattern routes
("{*path}", "*path") as literal paths, and ignored the version and the
global prefix exclusions. The dropped route was then covered by no
mount, and its handler ran without the middleware: "/docs/admin" next
to "/docs/:id.json", "/v2/accounts/me" next to "/v1/accounts/:id", or
"/users/me" excluded from the global prefix next to "/users/:id".

A route is now dropped only when it has no parameters or wildcards and
the parameterized route, compiled with path-to-regexp as the adapters
mount it, matches every path the route is mounted on, global prefix
and version included. A request matched by two routes that are now
both kept, such as "/files/a"
summary: Fixed later by d74ba14: fix(core): keep a controller root route next to an optional-tail route

request:
fix(core): keep a controller root route next to an optional-tail route

removeOverlappedRoutes() drops a static forRoutes() route when a
parameterized route of the same call matches every path it is mounted
on. It tested the mount path as listed, and the root route of a
controller is listed as "/invoices/" while the router serves it at
"/invoices". A sibling that needs the slash after its parameter
("/:tenant/{*page}", "/:tenant/*", "/a/{:id}") matches the former only,
so the root route was dropped and its handler ran without the
middleware, e.g. "@Get()" next to "@Get('{:id}')" in one controller.

Both sides are now compared without the trailing slash, as the router
serves them. "/invoices/" next to "/:tenant/" is still deduplicated.

A request for "/invoices/" now matches both mounts, so the middleware
runs twice for that spelling.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-AZLA1GUP.

request:
fix(fastify): apply middleware to plugins registered before init

NestFactory.create() registers @fastify/middie before main.ts runs, and
middie gives each new encapsulated context a copy of the middleware of
its parent as it is at that time. A plugin registered with an awaited
register() before app.init() therefore got a context without the
middleware app.init() registers through MiddlewareConsumer, so its
routes ran without it, unlike with a register() that is not awaited or
with Test.createNestApplication().

The adapter now tracks the contexts created since middie was registered
and also registers each such middleware in them, without its path, then
matches the path and strips it from req.url itself, as middie does.
Routes of plugins registered before app.init() now run the middleware
bound to their paths. In those contexts it runs after the plugin's own
middleware, and app.use() middleware added after the register() still
does not reach them.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner
summary: Fixed later by b1ee538: fix(fastify): track plugin contexts when the app registers middie

request:
fix(fastify): track plugin contexts when the app registers middie

With skipMiddie the application registers @fastify/middie itself, so
the adapter never ran registerMiddie() and never tracked the
encapsulated contexts created after it. A plugin registered with an
awaited register() before app.init() then kept middie's copy of the
root middleware as it was at that time, and the middleware bound
through MiddlewareConsumer at init did not run for its routes.

With skipMiddie, the adapter now tracks the contexts from its
creation, and registers each middleware in those that have a use() of
their own. A context created before middie shares the middleware of
the root, which already runs it.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-KMEXG4QO.

request: fix(core): roll back modules on failed lazy load (#18385)
summary: Fixed later by 93ce700: fix(core): build a lazy module once when loads overlap

request:
fix(core): build a lazy module once when loads overlap

LazyModuleLoader#load() builds every module its scan returns that no
concurrent load() is building. The scan is asynchronous, and it skips
only the modules that were already instantiated when it reached them,
while a module leaves the in-flight map as soon as its build finishes.
A module that a concurrent load() built completely during the scan
(e.g., a shared import of two lazy modules loaded at once) was
therefore built again, so its singletons got a second instance. When
such a scan then failed, its rollback also removed that module from the
container.

Modules that are already instantiated are no longer built again, and a
failed scan no longer removes modules that another load() is building
or has built.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as bug ANT-2026-3U5QLZFY.
summary: fix(core): build a lazy module once when loads overlap

request:
fix(core): leave early sse errors to the exception filters

Since 958ff952c, sse() lets the pipe from the SseStream end the
response, so that the response ends once the stream is flushed. When
the producer failed before any header was committed, for example a pipe
rejecting a query param while an interceptor is bound, the error path
ended the stream and the pipe then ended the response with an empty
200. An exception filter that awaited anything before writing found the
response already sent; on Express, one that did not check headersSent
then threw from a promise nothing handles, which ended the process.

fix(core): catch what the teardown of an sse producer throws

sse() unsubscribes from the route's Observable when the client
disconnects, once a HEAD response is complete, and when the producer
fails before the headers are sent. Unsubscribing runs the producer's
teardown (and the finalize() of an interceptor), and rxjs rethrows what
that throws as an UnsubscriptionError. As this ran from a socket 'close'
listener or a timer, outside of the handler's promise chain, nothing
caught it and the process exited.

The error is now caught and logged at each of these places, so the
response still ends and the request settles. A teardown that throws
when the producer completes or fails by itself is still thrown by rxjs
on the producer's own stack, as on any other route.

fix(common): reject arrays and primitives for validated classes

When plainToInstance() returned no instance of the class, ValidationPipe
validated a stand-in: the array itself, or an empty object for a
primitive. A stand-in has none of the class's properties set, so with
only optional rules (as in any PartialType DTO) or with
skipMissingProperties, an array-wrapped body or a primitive reached the
handler unchecked. ParseArrayPipe validates class items the same way,
so nested arrays and primitive items got through.

Such a value is now rejected through the exception factory, with the
message "Validation failed (object is expected)", when the class has
validation rules. Behaviour change: an array or a primitive sent for an
all-optional DTO now gets a 400. Errors found by the stand-in validation
still come first and are unchanged, and classes without rules, as well
as objects that a custom transformerPackage turns into plain objects,
are handled as before.

request:
fix(common): reject a buffer sent in place of a validated class

class-transformer copies a Buffer as it is instead of building the class
from it, so ValidationPipe validated the Buffer itself, which has none
of the properties of the class. Like the arrays and primitives that
197371c1f3 rejects, a Buffer sent as the whole value (e.g. a socket.io
binary attachment or a raw body) then passed any class without a
required property. The pipe also left the "constructor" key that it sets
on such a value (or on an array) for validation, so a handler that
copied the value into an entity made class-transformer apply the rules
of the validated class instead of the entity's, including which fields
@Exclude() hides.

A binary value is now rejected with "Validation failed (object is
expected)" when the class has validation rules, and the "constructor"
key is removed once the value is validated. Behaviour change: a Buffer
sent for a class with only optional rules now gets a 400.

request:
fix(microservices): only emit rmq replies that a request waits for

ClientRMQ used the correlation id of every message on its reply queue as
an event name on its response emitter. Whoever publishes to that queue
chooses the id, and an "error" event with no listener makes emit() throw
inside amqplib's dispatch, which closes the channel and the connection.
Requests in flight then never got their replies, and new ones failed
until the client had reconnected.

A message is now emitted only when a pending request listens for its
correlation id. Messages with any other id, which no request received
before either, are dropped before they reach the emitter.
